name: Surreal
basis: an art movement's idea rendered as a downward melt warp, dream grade and second sun (how)

lumenary.blurb: A dream version of the scene: it melts downward under a pale sun and drifting clouds.

facts.bestOn: Landscapes and interiors with clear horizontal structure

why: Surrealist painters took familiar things and bent their rules, as in a dream. Here the rule that bends is solidity: the whole picture slides downward like warm wax, more at the bottom, and a pale second sun hangs in a tinted sky. Because the melting varies smoothly from side to side, the drips look organic instead of random.
how: For every pixel, read the colour from a point higher up in the original, so the picture appears to slide down.
Let the slide grow towards the bottom of the picture.
Vary the slide from column to column using smooth value noise, with the drip width setting the noise scale.
Tint the colours towards a dream grade, more at the top than the bottom.
Draw a pale second sun with a halo and faint reflection, and a few flat-bottomed clouds.
history: Surrealism was launched by André Breton’s 1924 manifesto in Paris and drew on dreams and the unconscious. Salvador Dalí’s The Persistence of Memory (1931), with its soft watches, is the best known image of the melting idea, while Magritte and Max Ernst explored other ways of making the familiar strange.
uses: Editorial illustration about dreams, sleep or anxiety
terms: Moving where each pixel is read from, so the picture appears to shift or bend.
Smooth random variation made by blending random values placed on a grid.
A deliberate shift of colours to set a mood.
paragraphs: The picture melts. Every pixel is drawn from a point higher up in the original, so the image appears to slide downwards, and the slide grows towards the bottom. How far a column slides varies smoothly from side to side because it is driven by value noise; the drips slider changes the width of the noise, so more drips means narrower tongues.
A dream grade pulls the colours toward a tint, more at the top (sky) than the bottom, then a pale second sun with a halo and a faint reflection and a few flat-bottomed clouds are drawn on top.

equations.note: How far the pixel is pulled down. A = melt × 0.34 H, S is smoothstep and n₁, n₂ are value noise at two scales.
The colour grade: T is the tint, S(t) the sky colour at height t.

presets.text: Full melt with narrow drips gives a dripping curtain of colour.
A moonlit grade without the second sun feels quieter.
Gentle melt with heavy clouds is more of a daydream.
